study.question: Does replacing event-multiplicity weighting by distinct encoded field-key weighting within each match group improve the incumbent readout, and does that effect depend on target versus history-context queries?
study.hypothesis: Source inspection of accepted candidate.py (SHA256 ae07cfc238a702f3f917d2376779341d41249be731de3878c1e3b17e6b8545a4) shows equal match-group mass but event-level softmax inside groups. Repeated identical field/action/log-recency keys get multiplicity times exp(score), although their scorer inputs and read values are identical. This can overrepresent redundant coarse-key events; no observed dataset duplication rate is yet supplied, so its practical consequence remains a hypothesis. For each field read subtract log(m), where m counts that exact (match group, field ID, action ID, inherited fine recency bucket) key in the supplied prefix. This gives each distinct encoded key mass proportional to exp(score), preserving equal occupied-group mass. Keep original count features and the global norm reference, so this is only a change in retrieval measure, not a claim that frequency or full-model duplication sensitivity is harmful. Incumbent AUC0.6202303848951921 beats paired_match0.6191087654101018 and target_separate0.6153351063827704; latest coupled keys0.6198963511820914/0.6198384600666017 did not beat incumbent, despite nonzero swap sensitivity. Those negative trajectories motivate a different mechanism, not another coupling claim.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit target-related nonlinear scoring. DIN explicitly abandons softmax to preserve interest intensity; local reference already differs by normalized group attention. Proposed correction removes multiplicity only from the appended readout; original count features and norm reference remain. DIN supplies an opposing plausible explanation that repetition is useful, not evidence that this correction works. Not an exact DIN reproduction or a verified priority claim.

Change the within-group base measure through exact key multiplicity, without changing any learned shapes, queries, keys, values, group masses or classifier. Existing normalization, magnitude, slots, interactions and joint-key variants did not test this exact within-group repetition correction.

nearest_work.difference: Prior density variant changed BETWEEN-group mass using mean exp(score), holding within-group conditional weights fixed; it lost target AUC. Here BETWEEN-group mass stays equal and only within-group weights change according to exact repeated encoded keys. Prior failure does not refute this mechanism.

Joint event-key access was executed but reduced target and context AUC; its diagnostic sensitivity was not utility. Proposed variant retains separate scorer keys and addresses redundant key multiplicity. Industry usage was declared considered/unresolved rather than an implemented reproduction. No novelty established by the empty search indexes.

inherited_components: all frozen paired_match static/group means, four count statistics and 64 observed action-age histogram cells
shared category/brand embeddings, action and log-recency embeddings
DIN-style relation scorer and separate field values
norm matching to inherited global pooled history
unchanged classifier, initialization allocation, loss and optimizer
study.proposed_difference: Within each field read, define exact integer key (((field_id*5+action_id)*33+recency_bucket)*4+match_group). Masked positions are excluded. Count keys independently per impression using sort/run IDs/scatter, with no global vocabulary or other impressions. Use score - 1[key_measure=distinct]*log(count) before inherited group softmax. Event controls compute the same counts and use zero correction. Counts are based on discrete visible IDs, not learned equality, labels or predictions. Missing field0 remains an allowed encoded key but never a semantic target match. No new learned parameters. O(B L log L) preprocessing and O(B L) storage avoid pairwise L-squared memory. Preserve frozen 128-event limit; diagnostics may form a 129-event counterfactual only, never a training input.
predictions: Source-level mechanism: with query and membership held fixed, duplicating an identical encoded field key changes event measure but leaves distinct-key aggregate mass and raw readout unchanged within floating tolerance. Full logits are intentionally not invariant because original counts/pools and global reference norm remain frequency sensitive; context query itself may also change.

First512 label-free diagnostics quantify repeated-key event fraction, distinct counts per field, multiplicity and correction sensitivity. All-unique histories must give identical event/distinct readouts; all-identical keys within a group also give the same raw value. If no mixed repeated/unique keys occur, no practical correction opportunity is supported.

Primary prospective utility: distinct_target exceeds event_target and both frozen source bests at matched full-data recipe; compare incumbent directly as utility anchor. Secondary logloss and measured training/inference cost must accompany AUC. No minimum detectable gain or significance is claimed from seed42 alone.

Factorial conditioning: compare distinct_target-distinct_context with event_target-event_context. A positive correction effect common to both query sources supports only a measure change; added target-conditioning utility requires a repeatable target-versus-context contrast, accounting for seed variation.

Original features, parameter count, padding behavior, permutation invariance, empty/zero-length finite logits, group mass and norm identity must remain intact. Event_target should reproduce incumbent seed42 AUC/logloss; differences require investigation before causal interpretation.
falsifiers: Incorrect counts, nonzero padding mass, broken group mass, nonfinite outputs or changed original features invalidate implementation evidence.
Failure of fixed-query raw duplication invariance or all-unique event/distinct equality falsifies the proposed algebra/implementation, not merely utility.

Distinct variants not improving their event controls leave the utility of this implementation unsupported. Failure to beat paired_match or incumbent precludes replacing them. Negative trials remain preserved.
Gains shared by target-independent queries leave additional conditioning unsupported; sensitivity alone cannot establish either mechanism benefit or priority.

If repeated-key rates are negligible, or effects reverse across paired seeds, the hypothesized consequential redundancy is unsupported in this setting. One losing implementation does not refute all multiplicity-aware models.
Higher cost without a supported quality-cost improvement defeats an efficiency claim; matched preprocessing controls alone do not establish equal measured compute.
alternative_explanations: Repeated coarse keys may represent true interest intensity; DIN explicitly motivates preserving it. Correction can destroy useful frequency information even when original counts remain.
Hash collisions and coarse categories/brands can conflate distinct real events; no raw item identity is available or invented.
Changing softmax measure changes gradients/regularization and conditioning as well as redundancy; improvement alone does not identify a semantic mechanism.
Norm reference and history-context query remain multiplicity dependent, limiting duplication invariance to fixed-query raw retrieval.
Validation reuse, seed42 initialization and checkpoint selection may explain small differences; deterministic same-seed reruns are not repetitions.
Sorting/preprocessing adds wall time and may differ in host kernels despite equal shapes; parameter parity is not cost parity.
